sections.title: Executive summary

sections.title: Observed evidence
sections.text:
Revenue, orders and conversion versus baseline: Over 158 h ending 2026-10-11T00:00:00.000Z: 352 orders, net revenue £38276.38, 15865 sessions, conversion 2.22%. Baseline (82 h): hourly revenue +55.9% change, hourly orders +57.5%, hourly sessions +77.3%. Decomposition: sessions share 1.289, conversion share -0.267, AOV share -0.022 of the revenue change. Values are simulated business records; this describes what changed, not why.

Campaign performance versus baseline and peers: 5 campaign(s) analysed over 158 h ending 2026-10-11T00:00:00.000Z: CTR 1.92%, spend £3095.03, 140 attributed orders, CPA £22.11, ROAS 4.94. Versus baseline: CTR -1.7%, hourly spend +6.8%, hourly attributed orders +0.9%. Observations are simulated ad-platform records; frequency and CTR describe exposure and response, not intent.

Inventory levels, depletion and demand velocity: 1 product(s) observed to 2026-10-11T00:00:00.000Z: 1 at zero available units, 0 projected to run out within 72 h at current velocity, 98 units depleted in the 158 h window, 19 out-of-stock checkout failures. Out of stock: Nike Dunk Low Retro. Simulated inventory records derived from canonical inventory.level_changed events.

Review volume, low ratings and delivery complaints: 16 reviews over 158 h ending 2026-10-11T00:00:00.000Z: 0 rated ≤2 (0.0%), average rating 4.00, 2 mention delivery terms. Most low-rated products: Nike Dunk Low Retro (0/16). Simulated review records; delivery mentions are a keyword heuristic.

Delivery promise cohort and delayed orders: Cohort of 302 promises due in the 158 h ending 2026-10-11T00:00:00.000Z: 29 not delivered by promise (late rate 9.6%). Baseline late rate 8.7% on 23 promises (+10.4% change). 25 order(s) received a delayed status (average recorded delay 1933 min), 2 lost; 7 shipped order(s) are past promise with no delivered or lost event at the cutoff. Simulated fulfilment records; cohort membership is by promise due date, so immature promises never read as healthy.

sections.title: Competing explanations
sections.text:
stockout (moderate): The affected product was out of stock by the end of the observation window, with depletion and out-of-stock checkout failures recorded. This supports a stock constraint on some purchases, but does not establish that the constraint caused the demand increase; the timing of depletion relative to the surge is unknown.

viral demand (weak): Sessions and orders increased, which is consistent with increased demand, but the evidence does not identify social traffic or sharing as its source. Campaign-attributed orders were approximately flat per hour, so the available evidence does not establish a specific acquisition source.

ad inefficiency (weak): Campaign-attributed orders were approximately flat per hour while overall orders increased, and campaign efficiency measures weakened slightly against baseline. This may indicate limited paid contribution to the aggregate increase, but does not establish a material advertising failure or rule out advertising influence.

delivery delays (weak): Some orders were late, delayed, lost, or unresolved at the cutoff. The late rate was only slightly above baseline, and there is no evidence linking delivery outcomes to the demand increase.
